contacts.name: UK Emergency Services
contacts.notes: Police, Ambulance, Fire. Works from mobile — even with no signal strength shown in some networks.

contacts.name: European Emergency Number
contacts.notes: Also works in UK and throughout Europe; routes to 999 in GB.

circuitProtocol: At any UK race or track day event, follow circuit control and marshals immediately. Wave red flag = stop immediately and return to pits at reduced speed. Yellow flag = slow down, no overtaking. Incident reporting: inform circuit control / clerk of course; complete any ACU incident forms required.
raceEventEmergency: BSB and ACU events have dedicated circuit medical teams and FIM Grade medical centre requirements. At club and track day events, first aid is always present — location confirmed at rider briefing.
notes: 999 (or 112) for off-circuit emergencies. At public-road events (IOM TT, NW200, Oliver's Mount) follow event marshals and control procedures; road closures and re-opening schedules are strictly managed by organisers and local authorities.
